label: City of Rutland
header:
# City of Rutland municipal roster backfill -- Vermont
# municipal fan-out batch 20; issue #163 (VT master tracking).

sources.note: 24 App. V.S.A. ch. 9 (City of Rutland): section 2.1(a): the mayor is elected at the March election in odd-numbered years to a two-year term

City of Rutland, official election results for the March 3, 2026 city election (the clerk's official totals spreadsheet): Thomas Donahue won the 2026 mayoral election with 1,323 votes over David Allaire (1,000) and six others. The seat was filled for a ONE-YEAR term -- the remainder of the two-year term Mike Doenges won in March 2025 before departing mid-term; Doenges is not recorded as a holder
City of Rutland, official election results for the March 4, 2025 city election (the clerk's official results): Mike Doenges won the 2025 mayoral election with 2,075 votes

24 App. V.S.A. ch. 9 (City of Rutland): section 2.1(a): the City Treasurer is elected in odd-numbered years to a two-year term; section 10.6 makes the Treasurer ex officio Constable and Tax Collector, so no separate constable or tax collector post is created
City of Rutland, official election results for the March 4, 2025 city election (the clerk's official results): Mary Markowski was elected City Treasurer with 3,198 votes
Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Guide to Vermont's Town Clerks, Treasurers, and County Officials' (January 2026): lists Mary Markowski as Rutland City's City Treasurer
24 App. V.S.A. ch. 9 (City of Rutland): section 2.1(a): the City Assessor is elected in odd-numbered years to a two-year term
City of Rutland, official election results for the March 4, 2025 city election (the clerk's official results): Katie Burke Langlois was elected City Assessor with 2,913 votes
City of Rutland, Assessor's Office page (rutlandcity.org): Katie Burke Langlois is the City Assessor
24 App. V.S.A. ch. 9 (City of Rutland): section 15.2: the Mayor appoints the City Clerk (two-year term, in March of odd-numbered years)
Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Guide to Vermont's Town Clerks, Treasurers, and County Officials' (January 2026): lists Tracy Kapusta as Rutland City's City Clerk

offices.title: Alderman
offices.org_name: City of Rutland Board of Aldermen

sources.note: 24 App. V.S.A. ch. 9 (City of Rutland): sections 2.1(a)-(b): six aldermen are elected in odd-numbered years and five in even-numbered years, each to two-year terms; section 15.7(a): a vacancy in an elective office is filled by mayoral appointment until the next annual meeting

City of Rutland, official election results for the March 4, 2025 city election (the clerk's official results): the 2025 aldermanic winners included David Allaire, Paul Clifford, Larry Cupoli, Bill Gillam, Jr., Thomas Donahue, and Kiana McClure

City of Rutland, official election results for the March 3, 2026 city election (the clerk's official totals spreadsheet): the five 2026 aldermanic winners were Alex Adams, Sharon Davis, Peter Franzoni, Anna Tadio, and Michael Talbott

City of Rutland, Board of Aldermen roster (rutlandcity.org): the sitting board is David Allaire (President), Paul Clifford, Larry Cupoli, and Bill Gillam, Jr. of the 2025 class (terms to March 2027); Alex Adams, Sharon Davis, Peter Franzoni, Anna Tadio, and Michael Talbott of the 2026 class (to March 2028); and Barry Beauchamp and Curt Esposito, seated in the 2025 class. Donahue vacated his aldermanic seat on winning the mayoralty and McClure departed; Beauchamp and Esposito won in neither certified election and hold the two seats by appointment under section 15.7(a). (The June 2026 Secretary of State directory still lists McClure -- stale.)

24 App. V.S.A. ch. 9 (City of Rutland): section 2.8: each ward elects a Ward Clerk at the even-year election, to a two-year term; the city has four wards (charter section 1.3 leaves ward boundaries to ordinance, and the city's 2026 ballots are issued for four wards)

City of Rutland, official election results for the March 3, 2026 city election (the clerk's official totals spreadsheet): the ward clerks elected in 2026 are Barbara Spaulding (Ward 1), Beth Kiernan (Ward 2), Anthony P. Romeo, Jr. (Ward 3), and Steve Reynolds (Ward 4)

offices.title: Inspector of Elections
offices.org_name: City of Rutland Inspectors of Elections

sources.note: 24 App. V.S.A. ch. 9 (City of Rutland): section 2.8: each ward elects a First, a Second, and a Third Inspector of Elections at the even-year election, to two-year terms -- twelve seats across four wards

City of Rutland, official election results for the March 3, 2026 city election (the clerk's official totals spreadsheet): the inspectors elected in 2026 are First Inspectors Gary Spaulding (Ward 1), Thomas A. Carpenter (Ward 2), Stephen A. Leach (Ward 3), and Judy A. Delpha (Ward 4); Second Inspectors Cynthia Sinos (Ward 2), Denise Caggige Leach (Ward 3), and Angela M. Rivers (Ward 4); and Third Inspector Becky Boggess (Ward 2). Four seats -- Ward 1 Second and Third, Ward 3 Third, and Ward 4 Third -- returned no winner (write-ins only) and are left unfilled
